chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and others, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from some of our companions, who said:

I wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan Ṣāḥib al-ʿAskar (عليه السلام): May I be made your ransom, what is the meaning of the saying of al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام), ‘Our hadith cannot be borne by a brought-near angel, nor by a sent prophet, nor by a believer whose heart Allah has tested for faith’?

So the reply came: The meaning of the saying of al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام), that neither an angel nor a prophet nor a believer can bear it, is that the angel cannot bear it until he conveys it to another angel, and the prophet cannot bear it until he conveys it to another prophet, and the believer cannot bear it until he conveys it to another believer.
So this is the meaning of the saying of my grandfather (عليه السلام).

key_terms.امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قَلْبَهُ لِلْإِيمَانِ: whose heart Allah has tested and prepared for faith
key_terms.حَدِيثُنَا: the teachings and narrations of the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام)
key_terms.لَا يَحْتَمِلُهُ: cannot bear or carry it alone
key_terms.مَلَكٌ مُقَرَّبٌ: an angel brought near to Allah in rank
key_terms.نَبِيٌّ مُرْسَلٌ: a prophet sent with divine mission
key_terms.يُخْرِجَهُ: to bring it forth, meaning to convey or transmit it

ai.seo_question: What does the saying ‘Our hadith cannot be borne by a brought-near angel, a sent prophet, or a tested believer’ mean?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the statement about the difficulty of bearing the hadith of the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام) refers to the need to transmit and share it, not an absolute inability to receive it. Even angels, prophets, and believers bear such knowledge by passing it on to others of their kind, showing the gravity and depth of these teachings.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya and others, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from one of our companions who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan Sahib Al-Askarasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! What is the meaning of the words of Al-Sadiqasws: ‘Ourasws Ahadeeth, none can bear it except for an Angel of Proximity, nor a Mursil Prophetas, nor a Momin whose heart Allahazwj has Tested for the Eman’?’.

So the answer came: ‘But rather, the meaning of the words of Al-Sadiqasws, i.e., neither can an Angel bear it, nor a Prophetas, nor a Momin, is that the Angel cannot bear it until he brings it out (narrates) to another Angel, and the Prophetas cannot bear it until heas brings it out to another Prophetas, and the Momin cannot bear it until he brings it out to another Momin.
So this is the meaning of the words of my<sup>asws</sup> grandfather<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya and others have narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from one of our people the following.

“I wrote to Imam al-Hassan al_’Askari (a.s.) saying, May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, what is the meaning of the following Hadith of Imam Ja‘far al-Sadiq (a.s.)? “Our Hadith (statements) are difficult and they become difficult. No one is capable to bear them not even an angel or a prophet who is also a messenger or a believer whose heart Allah has tested for faith.?”

The answer came as herein below. “The meaning of the words the truthful one ‘that angels, prophets and believers are not capable to accept them’ is that of the truthful one is that the angel does bear it until he deliver it to other angels. The prophet does noor bear it until he delivers it to another prophet and the believer does not bear it until he delivers to another believer.
This is the meaning of the words of my grandfather.”
